page: Oracle Cloud Infrastructure VM.Standard.E4.Flex.64-512 is a high-density, general-purpose virtual machine based on the x86_64 architecture. The instance is powered by an AMD EPYC 7J13 processor running at a baseline frequency of 2.55 GHz. It provisions 64 dedicated physical cores supporting simultaneous multithreading for a total of 128 dedicated vCPUs. Accompanying this processing array is 512 GB of system memory, maintaining a balanced ratio of 4 GB of RAM per vCPU.

Hardware configurations for this server type omit integrated local storage and discrete GPU accelerators. All persistent filesystem activities must be served by network-attached block storage volumes. Connectivity includes one complimentary public IPv4 address. Because the hardware avoids dedicated local NVMe drives and GPU hardware overhead, resource efficiency is concentrated entirely on raw compute and memory capacity across high-thread environments.

This server profile is structured for compute-heavy and concurrent enterprise tasks that require high vCPU counts without skewed memory or localized I/O footprints. Workload profiles that align with this topology include distributed microservices, parallel data processing, software compilation, batch compute pipelines, and large application servers.
description: Oracle Cloud Infrastructure VM.Standard.E4.Flex.64-512 is a large general-purpose virtual machine built on the x86_64 architecture. Driven by an AMD EPYC 7J13 processor operating at 2.55 GHz, this configuration provides 64 dedicated physical cores delivering 128 vCPUs alongside 512 GB of system memory, adhering to a 1:4 vCPU-to-RAM ratio. The instance contains no integrated local NVMe storage and relies entirely on external volumes for filesystem needs. Furthermore, it features no GPU hardware acceleration and includes one complimentary public IPv4 address. By dedicating full core allocations without bundling accelerator hardware or local disks, the configuration maximizes CPU throughput per unit of provisioned infrastructure. It is suited for parallel compute tasks, CI/CD compilation pipelines, enterprise backend applications, and horizontally distributed services.
